reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
Not a correction, just a question for my own understanding.

I'm assuming that several of the recursively referenced `Sandboxes` can each return a non-`boost::none` `adjustments (account, issuer, currency)`.  What kind of confidence do we have that all of them will return the same `adj->origBalance `?  If they can return different `adj->origBalance` values, how will that play in this code?

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body:
The `origBalance` is the balance from the ledger before any debits/credits to that trust line _on that payment sandbox_. So `orgBalance` in fact will be different on each level on the stack of sandboxes.

You ask how it pays into the code. We take the minimum of these values as a lower bound for our return value. The reason this is needed is:

1) Sometimes the original balance - all the debits is slightly larger than it should be due to loss of precision in the accumulated debits.
2) We already use the current balance as a lower bound, but the account may have received a credit, so that lower bound is too large.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
Thanks for the explanation.  I see it now.  The `minBal` is the smallest starting balance seen for this `(account, issuer, currency)` in any of the recursive `PaymentSandboxes`.  So you're finding the smallest post-computation balance regardless of the depth of PaymentSandboxes.  That looks right.

You might consider adding your explanation as a comment in the code.  Personally, I didn't know enough about `PaymentSandbox` internals to get what you were up to just by reading the code.
